subject: maths
title: Shapes, Direction and Movement - Faces, Corners and Turns

steps.title: Shapes keep their names
steps.prompt: Let us explore together!

options.label: One triangle has turned upside down. Are both still triangles?
These are the cube's flat faces shown separately. How many faces?
The robot faces up, then turns right without moving. Where does it face?

steps.hint: Compare sides and corners, not the direction the point faces.
steps.explanation: Notice unchanged shapes, all six cube faces and a robot turn.
steps.shortExplanation: Make, count or compare the objects. Explain what changed.

mathWorkshop.title: Shapes keep their names
mathWorkshop.goal: Notice unchanged shapes, all six cube faces and a robot turn.

tasks.prompt: One triangle has turned upside down. Are both still triangles?
tasks.feedback: Both still have three straight sides and three corners. Turning keeps the shape unchanged.
tasks.hint: Compare sides and corners, not the direction the point faces.

tasks.prompt: These are the cube's flat faces shown separately. How many faces?
tasks.feedback: A cube has six square faces. A single view of the cube hides some of them.
tasks.hint: Count all six named face pictures once, including the hidden back and bottom.

tasks.prompt: The robot faces up, then turns right without moving. Where does it face?
tasks.feedback: It faces right. Turning changes facing, while staying in the same place.
tasks.hint: The robot stays on its square. Imagine a right turn from up.

parentReview.en: Guided practice is ungraded. Completion records the child doing the activities, not a book-question score.

steps.title: Cube faces
steps.prompt: How many faces does a cube have?
steps.hint: Count each flat face of a dice once.
steps.explanation: A cube has 6 square faces.
steps.shortExplanation: A cube has 6 square faces.

steps.title: Cube corners
steps.prompt: How many corners does a cube have?
steps.hint: Count the top corners, then the bottom corners.
steps.explanation: A cube has 8 corners.
steps.shortExplanation: A cube has 8 corners.

steps.title: Turned shapes
steps.prompt: Are these the same shape?
steps.hint: Count the sides of each. Did turning change them?
steps.explanation: Both are triangles. Turning does not change the shape.
steps.shortExplanation: Both are triangles. Turning does not change the shape.

source.answerKeyText: Yes — both are triangles; one is just turned.

steps.title: Cylinder faces
steps.prompt: How many flat faces does a cylinder have?
steps.hint: Look at a tin: how many flat ends does it have?
steps.explanation: A cylinder has two flat circular faces.
steps.shortExplanation: A cylinder has two flat circular faces.

steps.title: Solid pattern
steps.prompt: sphere, cube, cube, sphere, cube, cube... What comes next?
steps.hint: Say the shapes aloud and find the part that repeats.
steps.explanation: The repeating part is sphere, cube, cube.
steps.shortExplanation: The repeating part is sphere, cube, cube.

steps.title: Circle hunt
steps.prompt: Which of these has the shape of a circle?
steps.hint: A circle is round and has no corners.
steps.explanation: A clock face is round like a circle. A book and a ruler are rectangles.
steps.shortExplanation: A clock face is round like a circle. A book and a ruler are rectangles.

source.answerKeyText: Any circle: a wheel, a swing seat top, the top of a bin, a clock.

steps.title: Flat or curved faces
steps.prompt: Sort the solid shapes by their faces.
steps.hint: Does the shape have a curved surface that can roll?
steps.explanation: Sphere, cylinder and cone have curved faces; the other shapes have only flat faces.
steps.shortExplanation: Sphere, cylinder and cone have curved faces; the other shapes have only flat faces.

source.answerKeyText: curved: sphere, cylinder, cone • only flat: cube, cuboid, pyramid

steps.title: Robot routes
steps.prompt: The robot faces up. Choose both routes that reach the star two spaces up and two right.

options.label: turn right, 2 forwards, turn left, 2 forwards

steps.hint: Choose a route and watch where the robot ends.
steps.explanation: Both selected routes finish two spaces up and two right of the start.
steps.shortExplanation: Both selected routes finish two spaces up and two right of the start.

source.answerKeyText:
2 forwards, turn right, 2 forwards. (Also correct: turn right, 2 forwards, turn left, 2
forwards.)

steps.title: Turning a shape
steps.prompt: A shape that is turned round...
steps.hint: Turn a triangle. Does it still have 3 sides?
steps.explanation: Turning does not change sides or corners, so the name stays.
steps.shortExplanation: Turning does not change sides or corners, so the name stays.

steps.title: Cone corners
steps.prompt: A cone has...
steps.hint: Where does a cone come to a point?
steps.explanation: A cone has one pointy corner at its top.
steps.shortExplanation: A cone has one pointy corner at its top.

steps.title: Sphere faces
steps.prompt: A sphere has...
steps.hint: Is a ball flat anywhere?
steps.explanation: A sphere has one curved face all the way round.
steps.shortExplanation: A sphere has one curved face all the way round.

steps.title: Cuboid faces
steps.prompt: A cuboid has...
steps.hint: Count the faces of a box: top, bottom and the sides.
steps.explanation: A box shape has a top, a bottom and four sides: 6 faces.
steps.shortExplanation: A box shape has a top, a bottom and four sides: 6 faces.

steps.title: Triangle sides
steps.prompt: A triangle has...
steps.hint: Touch each straight side of a triangle.
steps.explanation: A triangle has three straight sides.
steps.shortExplanation: A triangle has three straight sides.

steps.title: A tent shape
steps.prompt: What is this 3D shape called?
steps.hint: Look at the ends. Two triangles joined by rectangles make a prism.
steps.explanation: Its two ends are triangles joined by rectangles, so it is a triangular prism.
steps.shortExplanation: Its two ends are triangles joined by rectangles, so it is a triangular prism.

steps.title: Prism faces
steps.prompt: How many faces does a triangular prism have?
steps.hint: Count the 2 triangle ends, then the 3 rectangle sides.
steps.explanation: It has 2 triangle faces at the ends and 3 rectangle faces: 5 faces.
steps.shortExplanation: It has 2 triangle faces at the ends and 3 rectangle faces: 5 faces.

steps.title: Pyramid faces
steps.prompt: A square-based pyramid has a square at the bottom and triangles on the sides. How many faces does it have?
steps.hint: Count 1 square at the bottom and 4 triangles on the sides.
steps.explanation: 1 square face and 4 triangle faces make 5 faces.
steps.shortExplanation: 1 square face and 4 triangle faces make 5 faces.

steps.title: Turning shapes
steps.prompt: Which shapes look the same after a quarter turn?
steps.hint: Picture each shape turned onto its side. Does it look the same?
steps.explanation: A square and a circle look the same when turned. A long rectangle stands up and looks different.
steps.shortExplanation: A square and a circle look the same when turned.

steps.title: Turn and move
steps.prompt: The robot is in square A1, facing up. It turns right, then goes 2 squares forwards. Which square is it in now?
steps.hint: Turn first. Then count the squares one at a time.
steps.explanation: After turning right it faces along the row: A1, then B1, then C1.
steps.shortExplanation: After turning right it faces along the row: A1, then B1, then C1.

steps.title: Six sides
steps.prompt: Which shape has 6 straight sides?
steps.hint: Count the sides of each shape. Which one has 6?
steps.explanation: A hexagon has 6 straight sides; a pentagon has 5 and a triangle 3.
steps.shortExplanation: A hexagon has 6 straight sides; a pentagon has 5 and a triangle 3.

stickers.meaning: A flat or curved part of a solid shape.

homeActivities.text: Feel safe solid shapes in a bag and describe flat or curved faces. Mark each cube corner once. Give robot commands along a paper grid.
